sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Copying arrays might seem simple, but there are important details to master. Let's break it down!

• How to properly duplicate array contents
• The difference between shallow and deep copies
• Common mistakes to avoid when copying arrays

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you have a tray of cookies (your array). If you want to share them with a friend, you might:

• Point to the same tray (this is like copying the reference)
• Make a new tray with identical cookies (this is a proper copy)

In Java, arrays are objects, so simply assigning one array to another doesn't create a new copy - it just creates another reference to the same array!

• **Shallow Copy**: Creates a new array but shares the same elements
• **Deep Copy**: Creates a completely independent copy with new elements
• **Common Methods**: Using loops, `clone()`, or `System.arraycopy()`

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Copying Arrays works:

steps.title: Original Array
steps.description: We start with an array containing values [1, 2, 3]

steps.title: Bad Copy (Reference Only)
steps.description: This just creates another pointer to the same array - changes affect both!
steps.code:
int[] badCopy = original;
badCopy[0] = 99; // original[0] is now 99 too!

steps.title: Good Copy (New Array)
steps.description: This creates a completely independent copy - changes don't affect the original

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Arrays are objects - assignment copies references, not values
✓ Use `clone()`, `System.arraycopy()`, or loops for proper copies
✓ Primitive arrays can use simple copy methods
✓ Object arrays need special handling (deep copy)
✓ Always check array lengths match when copying

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Remember to create a new array first
Test your copies to ensure they're independent
donts: Don't use simple assignment (=) to copy arrays
Don't forget to handle object arrays differently
Don't assume `clone()` works for all cases
Don't ignore array bounds when copying
sections.protip: For object arrays, consider implementing `Cloneable` or using serialization for deep copies

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Copying Arrays used in real apps?

examples.how: Creating backup copies of image data before applying filters
Duplicating game state for undo/redo functionality
Preserving original datasets while performing transformations

problem.description: Write a method that takes an array of integers and returns a new independent copy. Then modify the copy and verify the original remains unchanged.
hints: Remember to create a new array first
Test by changing values in the copy
problem.explanation: We create a new array of the same length, then use System.arraycopy() to efficiently copy all elements. This creates a completely independent copy.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Copying arrays requires creating new array objects, not just new references
📌 Use System.arraycopy() or clone() for primitive arrays
📌 Practice creating independent copies to avoid bugs
📌 Ready to learn about passing arrays to methods next!
